title: EO scene
description: A cutscene for Endless Online servers and clients. `source` is what an editor authors; `compiled` is what servers and clients run. See README.md for the rules this schema can't express.

format.description: The format version. Runners refuse a version they don't know.

id.description: The scene's name, as EQF's PlayScene and $scene use it. The file is <id>.eoscene.json.

summary.description: What happens in the scene, in a sentence or two: for the story it's part of, and whoever writes the next scene.

kind.description: personal: one player watches, locked, with stand-ins for real NPCs. world: everyone in range sees real NPCs directed by the server.

map.description: The map the scene starts on. A personal scene can take the player to others with map cues.

instanced.description: personal: the player is out of the world while it plays. Other players don't see them and nothing reaches them; a map cue moves them unseen. For intros, memories and dreams.

timeOfDay.description: The time of day the scene plays at, whatever the server's clock says, as HH:MM. Leave it out to play at whatever time it is.

footsteps.description: The surface every walk sounds on, a step a tile: the sound set <surface>-step in the scenes folder's audio/sounds. A walk's or an actor's steps say otherwise.

duck.description: How loud the music stays while someone speaks or a choice is up, 0 to 1. Leave it out to keep it as it is.

cast.description: Everyone in the scene, by name.

npcId.description: An NPC's id in the ENF file (1-based).

tile.description: [x, y] on the map where it happens: the actor's, the scene's, or a map cue's.

stepMs.description: Time per tile. 400 is the fastest EO clients animate cleanly.

pose.description: An animation, from the sprite's frames: idle (standing, breathing if the graphic does), walk (the four-frame walk cycle), attack (the two attack frames) or, for the player, sit (on the ground: knocked down, or resting; idle stands them up). custom:<name> is a client's own animation.

audioName.description: A file in the scenes folder's audio/music or audio/sounds, without its extension (.ogg or .wav). A sound name may be a set: name-1, name-2... one picked each time.

steps.description: Footsteps: a surface (the sound set <surface>-step), or none.

role.description: npc: an NPC already on the map. extra: an NPC made for the scene. player: the player watching (personal scenes).

spawn.description: npc: the map file's NPC spawn entry, counted from 0.

npc.description: npc: the first live NPC with this ENF id on the map. extra: the ENF id to show.

at.description: Where the scene expects the actor when it starts. Extras and stand-ins appear here.

hidden.description: extra: not shown until an appear cue.

map.description: The map the actor starts on, when it isn't the scene's. The runner sets the actor up when the scene first arrives there.

steps.description: The footsteps this actor's walks make, over the scene's footsteps: a surface, or none.

stepVolume.description: How loud this actor's footsteps are, 0 to 1: softer feet, smaller creatures.

label.description: The name the dialogue box shows for this actor's lines, instead of the NPC's own (or 'You' for the player): Mr Blob A and Mr Blob B for two NPCs the game calls Blob.

wears.description: player: what they're seen wearing for the scene, by EIF item id: a weapon, shield, armour, hat and boots. Armour is made for one gender, so list one of each and each player wears theirs. Their own gear comes back when the scene ends.

compiled.description: What servers and clients run: cues in order, each starting once the cues it waits for are done.

by.description: The tool and version that compiled it.

uses.description: Every cue type in the scene, so a runner can refuse what it can't show.

after.description: Cues that must be done before this one starts. Only earlier ids, and only from the same branch.

branch.description: [choice cue id, option index]: this cue runs only if that option is picked, and not before it is.

note.description: A caption for people reading the file. Runners ignore it.

path.description: walk: each tile stepped onto, in order. Each is next to the one before, the first next to from.

face.description: walk: the direction to face on arrival.

idle.description: walk: the pose to loop after arriving. Default idle.

steps.description: walk: the surface its footsteps sound on, a step a tile, as compiled from the walk, its actor and the scene. None when it's left out.

stepVolume.description: walk: how loud its footsteps are, 0 to 1, as compiled from the walk and its actor. Full when it's left out.

pose.description: pose: the animation to play. walk: what loops while moving (default walk).

loop.description: pose: true loops it until changed; false plays it once, then idle. music: false plays the song once; it loops otherwise.

show.description: say: box is a dialogue box with the speaker's face; balloon is the chat balloon over their head.

wait.description: say: click waits for the player to close it; time waits ms.

branch.description: The branch the option opens, by the name stories and EQF use to wait on it.

sfx.description: sound: the game's sound effect by number (sfxNNN.wav), or a sound of the scene's by name.

song.description: music: the game's MIDI song by number, or a song of the scene's by name (audio/music).

stop.description: music: fade what's playing out over ms.

volume.description: music: the song's volume, reached over ms; with no song or stop, a new volume for what's playing. sound: its volume.

facing.description: appear, map: the way to face on arriving.

how.description: appear: fade or pop. leave: fade, vanish or death. map: fade or cut.

map.description: map: the map the player is taken to. appear: the map the actor appears on, when it isn't the one it's on.

door.description: leave: the warp next to the actor it goes through, on servers that send NPCs through warps.

source.description: What an editor authors. Runners never read it; only editors do.

markers.description: Named tiles, so clips can say 'the inn door' rather than coordinates.

tracks.description: The editor's rows, top to bottom: cast names plus camera, screen, dialogue and audio.

editor.description: The editor's own state: zoom, scroll, selection. Free-form.

clip.description: One block on a track. Clips hold the same fields as cues, but place walks with to and via instead of a baked path, and are anchored instead of listed.

start.description: at: ms from the start of the scene, or of the clip's branch. after: once that clip is done. with: when that clip starts. offset: ms later.

branch.description: The branch this clip belongs to, named by a choice clip's option.

to.description: walk: where to, by marker, tile, or near: the nearest free tile beside that cast member, wherever they are by then.

toward.description: face, or walk once it arrives: turn towards that cast member, wherever they are by then. A face clip with toward needs no dir.

via.description: walk: tiles the path must pass through, in order.

options.description: choice: each option names the branch it opens.
